10.1002_aenm.71734: Block copolymer electrolytes exhibit a complex interplay between self‐assembled morphology, ion transport, and mechanical properties under galvanostatic battery cycling. Here, we propose a novel operando methodology combining concurrent rheology and electrochemical measurements upon dc polarization for a lithium bis (trifluoromethanesulfonyl) imide (LiTFSI) doped polystyrene‐ block ‐poly (ethylene oxide) diblock copolymer electrolyte. Time‐resolved measurements of the viscoelastic and electrochemical responses to the galvanostatic stimulus permit to uncover the effective response of the block copolymer electrolyte, tracking ion transport‐mechanical‐morphological properties simultaneously. Corroborated by scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM) imaging, we observe the block copolymer transitioning from unperturbed, increasingly aligned lamellae to reorganized self‐assembled nanostructures as the applied current density approaches the limiting current and, beyond its onset, the nanomorphology evolves toward gyroid and hexagonal phases. The diffusion coefficients decrease as current density increases, which is attributed to concentration polarization phenomena. Lastly, this methodology identifies a direct coupling between interfacial electrochemical processes and mechanical properties, highlighting the intimate interplay between interfacial phenomena and rubbery plateau modulus upon current densities.
10.1021_acsami.5c24044: The oxygen evolution reaction (OER) is a critical half-reaction in electrochemical energy conversion, yet its sluggish kinetics poses a major barrier to commercialization. Therefore, the development of efficient and stable electrocatalysts for the OER is one of the key measures to solve the energy shortage problem. The design of the catalyst is mainly concerned with its electronic structure. By adjusting the spin state of the active center of the electrocatalyst, the hybrid strength of the active center-ligand bond can be directly affected, and the adsorption strength of the reaction intermediate can be adjusted, so as to improve the activity of the catalyst. In this review, we discuss the importance of regulating the spin state of the active center. The latest strategies, mechanisms, and characterization methods to achieve spin state manipulation are then explored. Subsequently, the progress of the application of spin state modulation in the OER is discussed in depth, and the challenges of current research are analyzed. The necessity of combining density functional theory (DFT) with artificial intelligence (AI) for more precise modulation of spin state was proposed to promote the design and development of high-efficiency and stable OER catalysts to help the development of sustainable energy technologies.
10.1021_acsami.6c03703: Production of value-added C2+ products is an important topic in the research of electrochemical CO2 reduction reaction (CO2RR), and in situ spectroscopy identifies key intermediates and provides important details for a deeper understanding of the reaction mechanism. Applying a "borrowing" surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy (SERS) strategy, core-shell Au@Cu2O nanocatalysts with different shell thickness were used to probe the CO2RR pathways on the surface of Cu2O in both neutral (KHCO3 + KCl) and alkaline (KOH) electrolytes. In situ Raman spectroscopic measurements showed that the SERS effect occurs at the apparent shell thicknesses of up to 100 nm. Comparative analysis uncovers the correlation between low-frequency-binding (LFB) and high-frequency-binding (HFB) *CO intermediates and electrochemical selectivity. A higher *COLFB/*COHFB ratio favors the generation of C2H4, while abundant *COHFB leads to predominant CO formation.
10.1038_s41467-026-71930-x: Steel corrosion in marine concrete structures is critically exacerbated by solar heating and seawater penetration, accelerating chloride ingress and electrochemical degradation. Existing strategies often fail to synergize efficient thermal regulation and anti-wetting functionality for costal structures protection. To address this limitation, we develop a double-effect protective bi-coating, consisting of a carbonated dicalcium silicate (C 2 S)/BaSO 4 composite gel overlaid with a layer of hydrophobic SiO 2 nanoparticles, designed to passively suppress thermal and chemical corrosion drivers. The carbonation-activated C 2 S forms a chemically bonded calcium-modified silicate gel matrix, ensuring robust concrete adhesion, while BaSO 4 nanoparticles enhance solar reflectance (94.6%) and mid-infrared emittance (92.8%), enabling efficient passive cooling. Integrated with the hydrophobic overlayer for waterproofing, this protective bi-coating achieves a sub-ambient cooling (4.13 °C) under direct sunlight and excellent anti-wetting property (water contact angle of 151.3°), effectively mitigating solar thermal loading and chloride penetration. Furthermore, after 30 days of cyclic solar illumination-salt spray exposure, the protective layer can significantly reduce corrosion initiation time and current density, demonstrating double-effect protection for reinforced concrete through ion-blocking and cooling-enabled corrosion buffering. This work pioneers a passive strategy that synergizes radiative cooling, chemical compatibility, and ion-blocking functionality to extend the service life of marine infrastructure under coupled thermo-chemo degradation.
10.1038_s43247-026-04077-8: Impact-based flood-damage assessment integrates hydrometeorological information with vulnerability and exposure data to generate comprehensive evaluation of flood damage. This study uses the Integrated Land Simulator to assemble an impact-based flood-damage assessment framework for Typhoon Hagibis (2019), one of the most powerful typhoons to strike Japan in recent years. To systematically evaluate how typhoon-track position and levee height influence flood damage, we conduct longitudinal typhoon-track perturbation experiments and levee-height variation scenario analyses. Here we show that the flood damage is highly sensitive to small typhoon-track shifts, with a 0.2° longitudinal shift causing an average damage difference of 83.3 billion JPY. A 1.0° eastward shift causes the highest damage in Kanto and across Japan, mainly around Tokyo, while 1.6° and 0.4° westward shifts produce the greatest damage in Kinki and Chubu, mainly around Osaka and Nagoya, respectively. The levee-height sensitivity experiments show an average flood-damage reduction of approximately 9.1 billion JPY for each 10% increase in levee height.
10.1109_tmtt.2026.3672121: This article presents an improved theory and design methodology for single-phase unidirectional transducers (SPUDTs), developed through systematic analysis of electrical reflections from multiple electrodes to significantly enhance unidirectionality. It is compatible with all reflection-electrode-grounded SPUDTs and supports diverse piezoelectric materials and acoustic modes. Leveraging the Lamb wave S0mode in LiNbO3thin films, the improved DART (IDART) demonstrates over five times the unidirectionality of conventional designs for 10-period transducers. Transmission line experiments with IDARTs achieve a 7.9% 3-dB bandwidth at 3 GHz, with insertion losses of 5.9 dB at room temperature and 4.9 dB at 50 K, reducing losses by up to 1.2 dB compared to conventional DART. Also, the improved EWC-SPUDT (IEWC-SPUDT) offers advantages over conventional designs. Both simulations and experiments confirm the superiority of our SPUDTs in terms of unidirectionality, bandwidth, and in-band ripple. This new discovery and innovation, stemming from a reexamination of the classical SPUDT theory, are expected to systematically enhance the performance of microwave acoustic devices that rely on SPUDTs, including filters, delay lines, and sensors.
